Key Takeaways

Super Micro Computer fell 10% today with no company news, as AI hardware selling continued after Democrats' midterm wins.

Celestica, ASE Technology and Everpure fell harder on fears that data center building could slow.

Two days earlier, Super Micro raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $72 billion to $82 billion.

At less than half its usual forward P/E, Super Micro is priced for a slowdown, though its cash burn is a real risk.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) stock fell 10% today, and nothing the company said explains it. The AI hardware selloff that began Wednesday, after Democrats' bigger-than-expected midterm wins, deepened this morning.

Celestica (CLS) fell 13%, chip packager ASE Technology (ASX) dropped 17% and storage maker Everpure (P:NYSE) slid 15%, with no news of their own. All three sell into the same data center buildout.

Investors shrugged off a raised outlook

On Tuesday, Super Micro reported $19.9 billion of September-quarter revenue and raised its fiscal 2027 outlook (the year ending June 2027) to $72 billion to $82 billion. Going in, analysts expected $70.3 billion for fiscal 2027 and $81.7 billion for fiscal 2028:

Super Micro Computer (SMCI): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (years to June) (TIKR)

So the top of the new range is about what analysts had penciled in for a year later.

Investors are worried about Texas

Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who promised a data center moratorium, unseated Texas Gov. Greg Abbott on Tuesday. Texas holds more than a quarter of the US data center capacity planned through 2030, according to Yahoo Finance. Data center developer Applied Digital (APLD:NASDAQ) fell 16% today on fears about permits.

Super Micro needs its biggest customers to keep building: one made up 44% of September-quarter revenue. Inventory rose to $15.1 billion at Sept. 30, from $12.9 billion in June.

Investors sold the suppliers too

Late last month, Celestica reported third-quarter revenue of $5.83 billion, up 83%, and set a $40 billion revenue target for 2027. Investors sold it anyway. ASE and Everpure fell with rival packagers and storage names. Their next reports will show whether orders are holding.

Near its cheapest in five years

At Monday's close, Super Micro traded at 6.4x forward earnings, less than half its five-year average of 15x:

title: SMCI Stock Falls 5.7% After Q1 Results: Should You Hold or Fold?
detail:
SMCI Stock Falls 5.7% After Q1 Results: Should You Hold or Fold?
Subham Roy

SMCI
INTC
AMD
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Super Micro Computer SMCI shares have lost 5.7% since it released its first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Nov. 3, 2026. The stock has plunged 31.9% in the past one month, underperforming the Zacks Computer- Storage Devices industry and the sector's decline of 13.2% and 24.7%, respectively.

SMCI One-Month Performance Chart
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The decline in stock price has led SMCI stock to trade at a discounted price-to-sales multiple of 0.27X, below its industry's P/S of 2.19X. The undervaluation is further substantiated by a Zacks Value Score of B.

SMCI Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Given these dynamics, investors are wondering if it's the right time to buy, sell or hold SMCI stock. Let's delve deeper into the fundamentals, growth drivers, competitive positioning, valuation and risks surrounding the company to better assess its long-term investment potential.

SMCI Stock Declines in Tune With the Broader Technology Market

The decline in SMCI's stock price has come amid a broader sell-off in AI-related stocks spanning hyperscalers, semiconductor companies and AI infrastructure providers, as investors increasingly question whether massive AI investments will generate sufficient returns. Since SMCI supplies its products to these infrastructure providers, SMCI's stock has also been affected.

Furthermore, the recent decline after the earnings can mainly be attributed to investors assessing the sustainability of its rapid revenue growth and the pressure on profitability. The company reported record net sales of $19.95 billion, up 298% year over year and 79% sequentially. However, gross margin declined to 12.7% from 17.5% in the preceding quarter, while non-GAAP gross margin fell 480 basis points sequentially to 12.8%.

Management attributed the decline primarily to an increase in AI-related revenue mix, which rose to 71% from 59% in the previous quarter. Large-scale AI data center deployments carry lower gross margins than the more diversified enterprise and channel businesses, while the recognition of certain lower-margin deferred revenues further weighed on profitability.

Investor concerns were also heightened by Super Micro Computer's high customer concentration. During the quarter, one large data center customer accounted for 44% of total revenue compared with 28% for fiscal 2026 as a whole. Additionally, two customers represented 49% and 17% of accounts receivable at the end of the quarter. However, Super Micro Computer's exposure to AI infrastructure continues to provide a powerful foundation for growth.

Key Takeaways

Dell fell another 11% today with no news of its own, as the tech sell-off that followed Democrats' midterm wins deepened.

Analysts expect Dell's earnings to more than double this fiscal year, yet its forward P/E is back near its 5-year average.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Super Micro Computer are falling too, on data center politics and memory costs.

Dell's Nov. 24 report has to show its $95 billion AI backlog holding.

Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) is down another 11% today, after an 8% drop on Wednesday, and it hasn't put out any news of its own.

It has company. Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE:NYSE) and Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) are each down 9%, as the sell-off that began after Democrats' larger-than-expected midterm wins deepens.

Two new worries for AI hardware

Texas voters elected a governor who has promised a moratorium on data center construction, and Texas holds more than 25% of planned US data center capacity through 2030, according to Yahoo Finance.

Memory is the other worry. Qualcomm issued a weak forecast after Wednesday's close as a memory shortage weighs on smartphone sales, and Micron Technology (MU:NASDAQ) is down 12% too.

Intel warned last week that memory prices are shrinking the PC market, while server CPU units grow more than 30% this year and next. Dell sits on both sides of that: PCs earned 19% of its segment operating income in the quarter ended July 31, and servers, storage and networking the rest.

Margins are the real question

Super Micro's September-quarter revenue nearly quadrupled from a year earlier to $19.9 billion, but its gross margin fell to 12.7% from 17.5% the quarter before.

HPE's Cloud & AI segment, by contrast, earned a 17.0% operating margin in its July quarter, up from 7.0% a year earlier. It reports later this month, just ahead of Dell, so its server margin is the first read on Dell's.

Supermicro headquarters in San Jose, By JHVEPhoto

With a market capitalization of approximately $20.6 billion, Super Micro Computer, Inc. (SMCI) is a global technology company founded in 1993. Based in San Jose, California, the company designs and manufactures energy-efficient servers, storage systems, and networking solutions for AI, cloud computing, data centers, and enterprise infrastructure.

Shares of this tech giant have significantly lagged the broader market over the past year. SMCI has declined 37.6% during this period, while the broader S&P 500 Index ($SPX) has rallied nearly 13.5%. The trend has persisted in 2026, with the stock rising only 1.1% year-to-date, compared with the index's 12.3% gain over the same period.

Narrowing the comparison, SMCI has also trailed the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK), which has climbed 20.1% over the past year and 22.6% year-to-date.

www.barchart.com

On Nov. 3, Super Micro Computer reported its Q1 FY2027 results, sending shares up 3.1% as both revenue and earnings exceeded analyst expectations. Net sales surged 297.5% year over year to a record $19.95 billion, reflecting strong demand for AI infrastructure. Non-GAAP net income per share jumped 417.1% to $1.81, while adjusted EBITDA climbed to $2.23 billion from $335 million. However, non-GAAP gross margin declined to 12.8% from 17.5% in the previous quarter.

Looking ahead, Super Micro Computer raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $72 billion to $82 billion from its previous outlook of $65 billion to $72 billion. For Q2 FY2027, the company expects net sales of $19.5 billion to $21.5 billion and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.66 to $1.90. The quarterly revenue forecast also exceeded analysts' expectations of $17.14 billion.

For the current fiscal year, ending in June 2027, analysts expect SMCI's EPS to increase 27.9% to $4.17 on a diluted basis. The company has beaten the consensus EPS estimate in each of the last four quarters, which is impressive.

Among the 20 analysts covering SMCI stock, the consensus is a "Hold." That's based on three "Strong Buys," two "Moderate Buys," 12 "Holds," one "Moderate Sell," and two "Strong Sells."

NetApp Up 62% in the Past Year: Should Investors Buy the Stock?

NetApp, Inc.'s NTAP shares have surged 62.2% in the past year compared to the Zacks Computer & Technology sector and the Zacks Computer- Storage Devices industry's growth of 8.1% and 137.3%, respectively. The S&P 500 composite is up 11.1% over the same time frame.

The company faces stiff competition from its peers such as Super Micro Computer, Inc. SMCI, Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company HPE and Seagate Technology Holdings plc STX. SMCI has lost 26.6% while HPE and STX have climbed 114.1% and 100%, respectively, in the past six months.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Let us take a closer look at NTAP's fundamentals, key growth drivers, competitive strengths and potential risks to determine whether the stock remains an attractive investment.

Robust Storage Demand and AI-Led Growth Opportunities

NetApp is gaining from accelerating adoption of its all-flash storage solutions as enterprises modernize infrastructure to support mission-critical and AI-intensive workloads. All-flash array revenues jumped 47% year over year to $1.31 billion in the fiscal first quarter, supported by demand for high-performance, low-latency and cyber-resilient storage. Growing interest in hybrid flash solutions further strengthens its ability to address diverse customer requirements.

NetApp is also capitalizing on expanding AI infrastructure investments as enterprises transition from experimentation to production-scale deployments. The company secured approximately 350 AI and data lake modernization deals during the quarter, with transaction sizes increasing as customers expanded their AI workloads. Significant agreements with Samsung Electronics, a public-sector organization deploying NetApp AFX with NVIDIA SuperPOD, and an Asian neocloud provider highlight growing adoption. These developments reinforce NetApp's competitive position in supporting GPU-intensive AI environments and advanced analytics.

Expanding Cloud Business and Strategic Acquisitions

NetApp is benefiting from increasing demand for cloud-native storage services and enterprise workload migrations. Public Cloud revenues grew 28% year over year to $206 million during the fiscal first quarter, supported by strong adoption of first-party and marketplace offerings. Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP and Azure NetApp Files are gaining traction as customers seek efficient VMware migrations and cloud modernization. Meanwhile, the Keystone storage-as-a-service business continues to witness robust growth, strengthening NetApp's recurring revenue opportunities.
